text: Hi, my name is Lance Wyler. I am a glitch based, collage based artist. I work in film, television, theater, large scale installations. I'm here at Art Basel with my studio in residence and just kind of exploring the potential of emergent technology with my art practice. There's a lot of interest when people come in because it's very different than what they encounter. You know, it's a dark corner. You know, they kind of walk in there, they're very inquisitive, you know, like, what's kind of going on here? And we'll start very much by having a conversation about the underlying story of the piece, the work, the art. And then that'll kind of bridge in and start to move into a larger conversation about where maybe art is headed, what does it mean to make use of this technology? And a lot of people are kind of like, why the blockchain? So then I take the time to explain how it actually is part of the artistic process. And what I'm doing, it's not just, you know, taking something and putting it on chain. It's kind of looking and saying, how can the work be able to explore this new terrain? We have a conversation about it creatively, and it comes from the art side. It opens people up and they're interested to learn more about how they might be able to apply it. I've had some great conversations. I always love when people challenge the technology. I think it's really important to have that because being critical around what something is helps you to break through and make something that could be even stronger. What's so amazing about art is the human connection that comes from it. So what I'm hopeful for is that the humanity aspect can help to shape the technology before the technology shapes us.
